methodological_rigor.justification: Large prospective INSCOC registry with 1067 patients (696 lymphoma, 371 leukemia) evaluating eight nutritional tools against OS, LOS, and QLQ-C30. Statistical analyses include Cox regression, time-dependent AUC, C-index, LASSO regression for biomarker selection, and subgroup analyses. Key methodological concerns: (1) the HMPG-SGA composite tool is developed and evaluated in the same dataset without independent external validation (authors acknowledge this limitation); (2) no training/test split or cross-validation; (3) no TNM staging data and authors explicitly note this absence; (4) multiplicity across multiple tools and endpoints without formal correction beyond individual Cox p-values; (5) the reported AUCs (0.47-0.62) are near chance level, and the improvement from 0.547 to 0.616 is modest and in-sample. Statistical reporting of HRs with 95% CIs is adequate but the absence of a held-out validation cohort substantially limits rigor for a biomarker/prediction model paper.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Prospective cohort within a registry mapping to Oxford LoE 2b. Clinical relevance is moderate—identifying that conventional nutritional tools have poor discrimination in hematologic malignancies (especially leukemia) is useful for clinical practice, and the proposed HMPG-SGA direction is plausible. However, the in-sample-only validation and modest AUC (~0.6) substantially limit near-term clinical applicability; the tool is explicitly framed as an exploratory index.

reporting_quality.justification: The study involves prediction model development, so TRIPOD is the most applicable standard. Key TRIPOD elements like variable selection, model specification (LASSO), performance metrics (AUC, C-index), and calibration are partially addressed, but internal validation with bootstrapping, calibration plots, and optimism correction are not reported. Subjective PG-SGA components and their biases are acknowledged. Data availability is limited to the INSCOC registry (ChiCTR1800020329 referenced), with no code or model coefficients shared; hence data availability score of 2. No explicit TRIPOD checklist.

novelty_literature.justification: Nutritional tools (PG-SGA, GLIM, NRS-2002, KPS) are all well-established, and composite indices (PNI, NLR, AGR, PAR) have been extensively used in oncology (refs 12, 13, 14, 16, 21-24). The study's novel contribution is the systematic head-to-head comparison of eight tools in a large hematologic-malignancy cohort and the preliminary HMPG-SGA construction. The negative finding (tools perform poorly in leukemia) is informative. However, the approach is methodologically familiar and the new tool lacks external validation, placing this as a meaningful but incremental extension.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is organized and readable but has noticeable language and stylistic issues: verbose phrasing, redundant rephrasing of the same points across sections, occasional awkward terms (e.g., 'Metabolic Demand', 'somatic protein reserves'), and some cramped results reporting. Many results refer to supplementary figures/tables (S1-S37) which obscures the main findings. Tables and figures are referenced consistently but the main text could be substantially tightened. Supplementary numbering appears internally inconsistent (Table S4/S5 cross-references).

key_strengths: Large prospective registry cohort (n=1067) with head-to-head comparison of eight nutritional assessment tools, among the most comprehensive in hematologic malignancies
Important negative finding that conventional tools show near-chance discrimination for OS in leukemia patients, motivating disease-specific assessment
Transparent LASSO-based biomarker selection identifying AGR, NLR, PAR as independent predictors
Triangulation across OS, LOS, and QLQ-C30 outcomes strengthens the consistency of findings
Explicit acknowledgment of in-sample HMPG-SGA construction and need for external validation
key_concerns: HMPG-SGA is developed and evaluated on the same dataset without train/test split, external validation, or optimism correction—a fundamental TRIPOD violation for a prediction model paper
Reported AUCs (0.547 original PG-SGA to 0.616 HMPG-SGA) are near chance; clinical applicability of a tool with AUC ~0.6 is questionable
Absence of TNM/disease-stage data and heterogeneous hematologic diagnoses (lymphoma/leukemia/other) pooled together limit interpretability
No calibration assessment, bootstrap confidence intervals, or decision curve analysis
No TRIPOD checklist; analytical code and model coefficients not shared
Many results pushed to ~37 supplementary figures/tables, obscuring main-text readability
chief_reviewer.rationale: Useful negative/descriptive finding about conventional nutritional tools in hematologic cancers and a reasonable exploratory direction with HMPG-SGA, but prediction-model methodology is insufficient; Tier 3 with major revisions requiring external validation, TRIPOD adherence, and a tightened main text.
